title: TaskCompletionSource
sub: Your own task, built from callbacks
cards/0/body: TaskCompletionSource<T> creates a Task<T> that you complete yourself: SetResult, SetException, SetCanceled. That's how you turn an old callback API into a clean await.
cards/1/options/0: Completes tcs.Task with a result, and everyone awaiting it continues
cards/1/options/2: Blocks the thread until there's a result
cards/1/explain: A task from TaskCompletionSource runs nothing by itself; something outside completes it.
cards/2/title: The catch: continuations run on your thread
cards/2/body:
By default, SetResult may run the waiters' continuations right inside itself: synchronously, on the thread that called it. If you're holding a lock at that moment, or you're inside another library's callback, you get surprise reentrancy and even deadlocks.

The RunContinuationsAsynchronously flag sends continuations to the pool instead.
cards/3/options/0: So the waiters' continuations don't run synchronously inside SetResult
cards/3/options/1: So the task runs on another thread
cards/3/explain: SetResult returns right away, and the continuations run separately.
cards/4/options/0: The event may fire twice: SetResult throws the second time, while TrySetResult returns false
cards/4/explain: Callbacks can repeat, but a task completes only once.
cards/5/q: Which line can leave the task hanging forever?
cards/5/explain: On an error, the task never completes. It needs tcs.TrySetException(e).
cards/6/q: How can you complete a TaskCompletionSource task? Select all that apply.
cards/6/explain: Plus the Try versions of all three.
cards/7/pairs/1/1: Complete it if not already completed
